text: . The head of the UN nuclear agency, Rafael Grossi, has said that global nuclear power capacity could more than triple by 2060. In the International Atomic Energy Agency’s annual report to the UN General Assembly,  Mr. Grossi said that this growth would be driven by electrification, AI-powered data centres and technology companies’ demand for reliable, carbon-free energy. He highlighted the growing role of nuclear power in strengthening energy security.Mr. Grossi also raised concerns about the nuclear programmes of Iran and North Korea, threats to nuclear safety caused by the war in Ukraine, and reports that other countries were considering acquiring nuclear weapons. Regarding Iran, he said that the necessary technical groundwork for a diplomatic agreement had been completed.

. President Droupadi Murmu has congratulated Sheetal Devi and Toman Kumar on winning the Gold Medal in the Para Compound Mixed Team Archery event at the Games. Yathiraj, on securing the Bronze Medal in Badminton Men’s Singles at the Asian Para Games. She also wished him the very best as he builds on this achievement and brings out the finest in the game.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into action through initiatives like GST Council.Introduced on 1STJuly, 2017, the Goods and Services Tax (GST) marked a significant milestone in India’s tax reform journey. By bringing multiple Central and State taxes under a unified framework, GST gave effect to the principle of One Nation, One Tax and paved the way for a more integrated and streamlined taxation system across the country. The proposals of the GST Council seek to create a more predictable and taxpayer-friendly GST registration framework. Under the next-generation GST reforms last year, the GST council had simplified the earlier four-tier structure of 5 per cent, 12 percent, 18 percent, 28 percent into a two tier structure of 5 percent and 18 percent. Addressing the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi today, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said that through GST, the government has transformed a complex web of taxes into a national market.Addressing media after the 58thGST Council meeting in New Delhi, Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said that the Council   recommended removing arrest powers under GST, raising the prosecution threshold from one crore to five crore rupees.Over the past nine years, standardised procedures and rationalised rates have supported greater transparency, accountability and economic growth and strengthened the vision of ‘Ek Bharat – Shreshtha Bharat’.

. India continued its impressive performance at the Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, as the country bagged 26 medals including 7 Gold, 4 Silver and 15 Bronze today. With this, India’s medal tally has risen to 88, including 21 Gold, 26 Silver and 41 Bronze. India is currently in 4th position in the medal tally.India swept the men’s high jump T63 event today with Shailesh Kumar winning Gold, Varun Bhati bagging silver and Rahul securing bronze.Dharmaraj Solairaj smashed the Asian record to clinch gold in the men’s T44/T62/T64 long jump combined event, successfully defending his title at the Asian Para Games. Dharmaraj set a new Asian record with a winning jump of 7.15 metres.Sprinter Anjanaben Bumbadiya struck gold in the women’s 400 metre T47 event. Bumbadiya clinched the gold with a time of 59.97 seconds and was followed by compatriot Jayanti Behera in second place.  In the women’s 400m T12 event, visually impaired Tejalben Damor won her second medal of the Games by finishing with a silver after clocking 57.60 seconds. Dilip Mahadu Gavit won the gold medal in men’s 400 metre T47 race, clocking 48.27 seconds.Suvarna Raj clinched a gold medal in the women’s F54 discus throw with a best effort of 15.66 metres.Armless archer Sheetal Devi reigned supreme in the women’s compound individual and mixed team events to claim gold in both competitions. She overcame a four-point deficit to defeat Singapore’s Alim Nur Syahidah 142-139 in a repeat of the Hangzhou 2023 final.Sheetal Devi and Toman Kumar bagged gold in the Archery compound mixed team event, defeating Indonesia’s Teodora Audi Ayudia Ferelly and Ken Swagumilang 151-148 in the final.Swati Chaudhary created history by winning India’s first-ever medal in the W-1 category, securing silver in the women’s individual event. She lost 4-6 to China’s Cen Mengkan in the final despite taking an early 4-2 lead.Bhavina Patel and Subham Wadhwa got a bronze medal in the mixed doubles XD7 Table Tennis competition.Kapil Kumar clinched the silver while Swatik Patil bagged the bronze medal in their respective swimming events.India also added several bronze medals in para-Badminton.Manisha Ramadass and Pramod Bhagat claimed bronze in mixed doubles after losing their semifinal to Indonesia’s Leani Ratri Oktila and Hikmat Ramadani.Sanjana Kumari secured bronze in women’s singles SL3, while Suhas Yathiraj and Abhijeet Sakhuja bagged bronze in men’s singles SL4. Krishna Nagar and Nithya Sre also got bronze in mixed doubles SH6.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into action through initiatives like the PM Jan Dhan Yojana.Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana has emerged as a cornerstone of India’s financial inclusion journey since its launch in 2014 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. With over 59 crore Jan Dhan accounts, the scheme has grown into the largest financial inclusion initiative in the world. The scheme has provided universal banking access for every household and has become the foundation for direct benefit transfers. It has helped save almost 3.5 lakh crore rupees by plugging leakages in welfare delivery.Addressing the centenary celebrations of Shri Ram College of Commerce in New Delhi last month, Prime Minister Narendra Modi had said that Jan Dhan Yojana has transformed India’s banking landscape and today almost every family in the country is connected to the banking system.As the world’s largest financial inclusion initiative, the scheme is redefining access to banking for millions of underprivileged citizens. The Jan Dhan account holder can avail overdraft facility of up to ten thousand rupees per household.

. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has urged financial sector regulators and other stakeholders to expedite the refund of unclaimed assets to their rightful owners. These include bank deposits, dividends, shares, post office savings, insurance proceeds and pension funds. Ms Sitharaman stated this while chairing the 30th meeting of the Financial Stability and Development Council (FSDC) in New Delhi yesterday. Ms Sitharaman also called for simplifying Know Your Customer (KYC) procedures and strengthening cybersecurity preparedness amid rising geopolitical uncertainties.The Council reviewed efforts under the ‘Your Money, Your Right’ campaign, which aims to facilitate the return of unclaimed financial assets to their rightful owners. It urged the concerned ministries and regulators to intensify their efforts to ensure timely refunds. The Council also deliberated on issues relating to macroeconomic and financial stability, as well as the country’s preparedness to address emerging challenges. Discussions included measures to promote innovation in the fintech sector and explore the potential of tokenisation of financial assets and other real-world assets.According to the Finance Ministry, the meeting also reviewed the country’s preparedness to protect critical information infrastructure, strengthen the resilience of security systems and enhance cybersecurity preparedness among Regional Rural Banks.In view of growing geopolitical challenges and global uncertainties, the Finance Minister called for more frequent meetings of the Council according to a predefined schedule.The meeting was attended by RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra, Chief Economic Adviser Dr V. Anantha Nageswaran, Secretary of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology S. Krishnan, and other senior officials.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued an orange alert for heavy to very heavy rainfall over Keralam, Mahe, Lakshadweep, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal today. The weather agency has also forecast heavy rainfall over the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and south interior Karnataka.According to the IMD, thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds are likely over Delhi, Haryana, Chandigarh, Punjab, Rajasthan, Konkan, Goa, Andhra Pradesh and Lakshadweep until tomorrow. The Met Department has forecast thunderstorms accompanied by lightning over coastal Karnataka today. Meanwhile, the weather agency has forecast mainly cloudy skies over the national capital today.

India’s para-athletes surpassed all expectations to deliver their best ever show, taking its overall tally to 114 medals, including 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze at the Asian Para Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan.Para Athlete Sumit Antil clinched gold medal in the men’s javelin throw F42-F44/F61-F64 final, while Mahendra Gurjar won Silver and Sandip Sanjay Sargar clinched bronze medal to complete a podium sweep for the country. Sumit, competing in the T64 category and supported under the Target Olympic Podium Scheme, registered a best throw of 72.46 metres to secure gold with 1 thousand 112 points. In Shooting, Mona Agarwal clinched gold in the women’s 50-metre rifle three positions SH1 event, setting a new world record with a score of 357.5 to claim her second gold medal of the Games.Pranav Soorma won the gold medal and set a new Asian Para Games Record in the Men’s Club Throw F51 event at with a throw of 32.87 meters. Indian para sprinter Sandeep wins bronze medal in men’s 100m T44 event. Para swimmer Himanshu Nandal wins bronze medal, adding another podium finish in the men’s 100m freestyle S11 event. Rakeshbhai Bhatt clinched the bronze medal in the men’s 200m T37 final. He clocked a time of 23.64 seconds to finish third on the podium. In Badminton, Thulasimathi Murugesan and Manasi Girishchandra Joshi beat China’s Yang Qiuxia and Xiao Zuxian to win the women’s doubles SL3-SU5 title. Naveen Sivakumar added the men’s singles SL4 gold, beating Indonesia’s Fredy Setiawan. Nitesh Kumar clinched the men’s singles SL3 gold beating compatriot Pramod Bhagat. Pramod had to settle for silver. Thulasimathi Murugesan and Nitesh Kumar have to settle for silver in the mixed doubles SL3-SU5 event after losing to Indonesia’s Leani Ratri Oktila and Hikmat Ramdani in the final.In para-athletics, Sandeep Kumar shattered the T44 world record with a time of 52.28 seconds to win gold in the men’s 400 metres, while Ajay Kumar secured bronze in the same event. Haney also struck gold in the men’s Javelin throw F37 event with a world-record effort of 60.49 metres. In Archery, Paralympic champion Harvinder Singh and his debuting partner Vijay Sundi clinched the men’s doubles gold medal, while India’s women’s doubles team settled for a silver in the recurve events.

The State Bank of India (SBI) has individually notified customers whose personal data was identified in a recent suspected cyber incident, assuring them that their account balances and funds remain safe. In a statement issued yesterday, the country’s largest public sector lender said, the affected customers have been informed. The bank also advised customers to follow safe digital banking practices and remain alert to suspicious calls, messages and emails. SBI initiated a detailed investigation after receiving alerts on 16th of this month from its Threat Intelligence Service Provider, the Defence Cyber Agency and the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) about suspected customer data exposure on the dark web.A preliminary analysis of around three lakh 75 thousand records identified 3,897 customer records containing personally identifiable information. The information reportedly included names, mobile numbers, email addresses, dates of birth and residential addresses. The bank immediately activated its cyber incident response and containment measures. It also appointed an independent cybersecurity agency empanelled by CERT-In to assess the incident and establish the nature and extent of the suspected data exposure.SBI clarified that the incident had no material impact on its business operations, financial performance or continuity. It said its core banking services continue to function normally without disruption. The bank has urged customers never to share their one-time passwords, PINs or banking passwords with anyone and to exercise caution while responding to unsolicited communications.

. Sheikh Theyab bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Deputy Chairman of the Presidential Court for Development and Fallen Heroes’ Affairs, UAE, met with Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi. The two sides discussed bilateral friendship and cooperation, and ways to strengthen ties. They also exchanged views on key issues like shifts in the global economy, the role of technology and artificial intelligence in advancing development, and the importance of international partnerships in turning global challenges into opportunities for growth and prosperity.The UAE delegation to New Delhi also included Abdulla bin Touq Al Marri, Minister of Economy and Tourism; Saeed bin Mubarak Al Hajeri, Minister of State; Abdulla Saif Al Nuaimi, UAE Ambassador to India and a number of senior UAE officials. Al Marri delivered the UAE’s address in the Summit and participated in a session titled “India and the UAE: Building Partnerships in a Changing Gulf”.Al Marri highlighted the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), signed in February 2022, as a milestone in bilateral economic relations. He said the agreement had helped drive trade growth, while the partnership had expanded into investment, logistics, energy, industry, payments, food security and advanced technology.The minister noted that non-oil trade between the UAE and India had risen by almost 50 percent in the last three years, from around USD 51 billion in the agreement’s first year to more than USD 76 billion in 2025. Total bilateral trade exceeded 101 billion in India’s last financial year, while the two countries have set a target of USD 200 billion in bilateral trade by 2030. He said the relationship had evolved beyond a conventional trading partnership into one that increasingly connects investment, financial services, infrastructure and emerging technologies.On innovation, Al Marri highlighted the complementary strengths of India and the UAE. India brings scale, skills and an exceptional digital ecosystem, while the UAE offers capital, infrastructure, energy and a strategic location connecting Asia with the Middle East, Africa and Europe. Citing recent investment developments, Al Marri pointed to plans of India-UAE cooperation for an integrated aluminium complex in Odisha valued at US$11.5 billion.Addressing the summit, Al Marri said the global economy was undergoing a period of transition, making partnerships built on trust, investment and practical cooperation increasingly important. He said the UAE-India relationship had become more important as the world grew increasingly turbulent, drawing on historical maritime links that predate formal economic agreements. “Between us and India lies a sea that our ancestors did not view as a challenge, but as a path,” he said, recalling how dhows carried spices, textiles and pearls between ports long before the concept of economic corridors emerged.Turning to the UAE’s economic outlook, Al Marri acknowledged the difficult conditions facing the Gulf region, while emphasising that the UAE’s openness remained a source of strength. He said economic resilience depended on building a diversified economic structure capable of absorbing disruption, rather than assuming that economies could remain immune to external shocks. He outlined priorities centred on productivity, innovation and structural transformation, stressing that economic performance should be assessed not simply by how much is produced, but by how much value is generated by every worker, company and dirham of capital. The UAE’s response, he said, involved accelerating the adoption of artificial intelligence, developing skills, strengthening competition and making it easier for growing companies to access finance.Addressing the changing global order, he argued that diplomatic goodwill alone could not guarantee resilience. Countries also needed infrastructure, investment and effective execution to translate partnerships into tangible economic outcomes. He cautioned against responding to global fragmentation with further fragmentation, describing diversification as a shield against economic fluctuations while emphasising that it could not replace partnerships founded on mutual trust.He said economic corridors needed to deliver practical commercial value rather than remain lines on a map. Such corridors require connected ports, coordinated customs authorities, available financing and companies that find it worthwhile to use them. Without these elements, he said, a corridor would remain merely a project.The minister also highlighted the contribution of the Indian community in the UAE, describing people as the most important bridge between the two countries. Millions of Indians have made the UAE their home and contributed to its economic development and it will never be forgotten, he said.

. Renowned Indian theoretical physicist Professor Ashoke Sen has been awarded the prestigious Oskar Klein Medal for 2026, becoming the first Indian physicist to receive the international honour. The award recognizes his pioneering contributions to string theory which seeks to explain the fundamental nature of the universe, black hole entropy and string field theory, which have significantly shaped modern theoretical physics.An alumnus of Presidency College in Kolkata and the University of Calcutta, Professor Sen has also been conferred the Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan for his contributions to science. He is currently serving as the Infosys-Madhava Chair Professor at the International Centre for Theoretical Sciences in Bengaluru.The Oskar Klein Medal is awarded annually by Stockholm University and the Nobel Committee for Physics of the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences in Sweden. Established in 1988, it honours distinguished contributions to physics and is named after Swedish theoretical physicist Oskar Klein. Previous recipients include Nobel laureates Stephen Hawking, Peter Higgs, Chen-Ning Yang, Steven Weinberg and Hans Bethe, underlining the award’s international standing.

Absconding gangster Himanshu Bhau, wanted in India for multiple murders and organised crime, and another fugitive Neeraj Faridpuria have been arrested by law enforcement agencies in the United States. The two were arrested together in Las Vegas on 22nd of October following inputs from the Haryana Special Task Force (STF). The action was carried out with the assistance of the US immigration enforcement agency (ICE). Haryana STF is in touch with US authorities and central agencies to secure their deportation to India.Himanshu Bhau, whose real name is Himanshu Ritoliya, hails from Rohtak in Haryana. He is a rival of jailed gangster Lawrence Bishnoi and was on the most-wanted lists of the Haryana and Delhi Police. Several cases, including murder, kidnapping and extortion, have been registered against him and his associates across Haryana, Delhi and Uttar Pradesh. An Interpol notice has also been issued against the notorious gangster in August 2023. According to the police, he obtained a passport using forged documents before leaving India.Neeraj Faridpuria, a resident of Haryana’s Palwal district, was also living in the US at the time of his arrest. More than 25 criminal cases have been registered against him.

In Asian markets today, China’s Shanghai Composite rose 0.9 per cent, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng gained 0.7 per cent, South Korea’s Kospi advanced 0.3 per cent, and Singapore’s Strait Times added 0.1 per cent. On the other hand, Japan’s Nikkei 225 lost 0.3 per cent, while markets in Taiwan remained closed for a holiday.On the economic front, Japan’s consumer price index (CPI) rose 2.1 per cent year on year in September, up from 1.9 per cent in August. . Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into action through initiatives like Give It Up Campaign.The Give It Up campaign, launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in 2015, has encouraged consumers to voluntarily give up their LPG subsidies. Under the campaign, more than one crore 13 lakh LPG consumers have voluntarily surrendered their LPG subsidy. The savings helped provide LPG connections to poor households under the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana, particularly benefiting rural women who relied on firewood and cow dung for cooking. The government has provided over ten crore 56 lakh free LPG connections under the scheme to adult women from poor households across the country. Addressing the Delhi Economics Conclave in 2015, Prime Minister Modi highlighted that the Give It Up movement inspired the citizens to come together to help underprivileged families acquire clean fuel.A resident of Uttar Pradesh, Sanju Devi said that the gas stove has made cooking much more convenient and freed her from exposure to smoke.The Give It Up campaign has promoted a sense of social responsibility among citizens and has supported the government’s efforts to ensure clean cooking fuel access for all.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into action through initiatives aimed at removing the colonial mindset.The history of modern India is deeply entangled with two centuries of British colonialism, and decades after Independence. Over the past few years, the Government has slowly been steering India, away from these vestiges of British rule. Addressing the nation from the Red Fort on the 76th Independence Day in 2022, the Prime Minister outlined five resolutions, or Panch Pran for the next 25 years. Elaborating on the second Praan, he said, in no part of citizens’ existence, not even in the deepest corners of mind or habits should there be any ounce of slavery.In a concerted effort to free the country from its colonial legacy and promote a distinct Indian identity, the Government has undertaken a series of initiatives across various sectors. the historic Rajpath in New Delhi was renamed Kartavya Path and inaugurated by the Prime Minister in 2022.  Similarly, a grand statue of freedom fighter Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose was installed near India Gate, which has replaced the statue of King George the Fifth. The Indian Navy also adopted a new ensign in 2022, replacing the earlier design that featured the Saint George’s Cross. The Government has merged the Rail Budget with the Union Budget from budget year 2017-18, ending a practice dating back to 1924. BJP leader Ram Madhav has said that restoring India’s cultural and civilizational identity is a symbol of self-respect. He added that decolonisation is the real patriotism that is happening today.The Government has further sought to revive literature banned during British rule, with the National Archives of India compiling a catalogue of banned poems, writings and publications from the freedom struggle. In addition, more than 1,500 obsolete laws have been repealed in recent years as part of efforts to simplify governance and remove outdated legal provisions.These initiatives reflect the Government’s stated commitment to building a confident, self-reliant India rooted in its cultural heritage and national values.

India has emerged as the third-largest exporter of arms to Europe, driven by rising demand for defence equipment under the European Union’s ‘ReArm Europe’ initiative and the expansion of the country’s domestic manufacturing sector. Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh made the remarks while talking to media persons yesterday. He said India’s defence exports have reached an all-time high of 38 thousand 424 crore rupees, equivalent to around 3.6 billion euros. He said the increase in exports to Europe was largely driven by the growing demand for standard ammunition, artillery shells and other large- and small-calibre ammunition.Mr Singh said, country’s defence manufacturing ecosystem has witnessed significant growth over the past decade. He said the sector comprises 16 major public sector companies, around 840 large and medium-sized private enterprises, and nearly 17 thousand small enterprises, including start-ups. He added that India now exports defence equipment to more than 80 countries. The country’s defence exports range from artillery and ammunition to small arms, helmets, bulletproof jackets and other tactical equipment.Mr Singh highlighted that the government aims to ensure that 75 per cent of annual defence capital expenditure, estimated at 20 to 25 billion dollars, is spent domestically, with priority given to Indian-designed, developed and manufactured products.The Defence Secretary also noted that Indian defence manufacturers are attracting interest from international buyers, particularly in Southeast Asia, for a wide range of defence equipment, including small arms, components and artillery gun systems.The Defence Secretary said India plans to expand its participation in European defence procurement through joint ventures with European partners, while also encouraging European companies to manufacture in India under the Make in India initiative. He said greater integration of Indian and European defence supply chains will help meet international demand and strengthen cooperation.

. India and Sri Lanka strengthened their cultural ties through the preservation of shared Buddhist heritage. The SAMHiTA Project -South Asian Manuscript Histories and Textual Archive was launched at Colombo’s Gangaramaya Temple, a project to digitize ancient manuscripts and preserve their historical and cultural knowledge. The project is undertaken by the India International Centre in New Delhi with grant assistance from the Government of India. Gangaramaya Temple is the first institution in Sri Lanka to partner with the initiative.Under an MoU signed in July this year, one hundred ancient manuscripts preserved at the temple are being digitized by a team of local experts. India is providing support to the initiative, with the digitization work expected to be completed by the end of November. The manuscripts preserve valuable knowledge relating to religious traditions, philosophy, languages and cultural practices.The initiative reflects the enduring Buddhist and civilizational links between India and Sri Lanka. By preserving these historical records in digital form, SAMHiTA seeks to safeguard an important part of South Asia’s shared heritage and encourage more institutions in Sri Lanka to join the effort.

. India’s business sentiment improved in the July-September quarter of this fiscal year after declining for four consecutive quarters. The Business Confidence Index rose to 107.8 from 99.8 in the previous quarter, according to the latest survey by the National Council of Applied Economic Research (NCAER).The survey, conducted in September among 502 firms across six cities, found improvement in all four indicators of business confidence. The share of firms expecting overall economic conditions to improve over the next six months rose to 50 per cent from 43 per cent. Expectations of improved financial positions increased to 41 per cent from 37 per cent, while the share viewing the investment climate positively rose to 30 per cent from 26 per cent. Firms expecting capacity utilisation to remain near or above optimal levels increased to 94 per cent from 91 per cent.NCAER survey indicated a broad-based recovery in sentiment among both micro, small and medium enterprises and large firms. The Business Confidence Index for MSMEs rose from 93 to 100, while that for large firms increased from 111.6 to 120.3. She added that business prospects had improved in both domestic and external markets, while cost sentiments had moderated.

Indian nationals had been advised to avoid areas where protests are taking place, exercise due caution while travelling and follow advisories issued by local authorities.
